verdict.rationale: Airbyte's own Terraform provider lets you automate and version-control Airbyte configuration as code. PyAirbyte offers a Python, code-first way to extract and load data, and connectors have a low-code YAML format underneath the Builder. However, the core product is UI- and server-centric (the no-code Connector Builder lives in the Airbyte UI), and the evidence only shows code representations layered on top, not pipelines that live natively as plain code in a repo. Missing for 10: evidence that whole pipelines live natively in a user repository as plain code, documented review/CI workflows, documented portability of pipeline definitions across deployments, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, my pipelines are plain code and config in my own repository — versioned, reviewed, and portable like any software

citations.quote: you can use Airbyte's Terraform provider to automate and version control your Airbyte configuration as code
Data can be extracted from sources and loaded into caches
It provides an intuitive user interface on top of the low-code YAML format
